items.title: Frank leading candidate for Palace job with Sage likely to be sacked
items.excerpt: Thomas Frank has emerged as a leading candidate to take over as Crystal Palace manager if the Eagles decide to sack Pierre Sage.
body: Thomas Frank has emerged as a leading candidate to take over as Crystal Palace manager if the Eagles decide to sack Pierre Sage.
Other candidates that Palace are interested in include Frank Lampard , Sean Dyche , Vitor Pereira , Kim Hellberg , Vitor Matos and Tony Popovic.
No decision has been taken at Palace yet, but Sage is likely to lose his position following a seventh league defeat of the season.

Frank is amongst a list of names that Palace considered in the summer. The former Brentford boss is expected to be among the frontrunners if as expected the club decide to make a managerial change. items.title: Man Utd in relegation zone but boss Carrick 'expects' to stay on
items.excerpt: Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick "expects" to stay on despite his side sitting in the relegation zone after Sunday's dramatic 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa.
body: Under-pressure Manchester United boss Michael Carrick "expects" to stay on despite his side sitting in the relegation zone after Sunday's dramatic 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa.
Man Utd scored twice in stoppage time to rescue an unlikely point against Villa, but the draw leaves Carrick's side third-bottom and a point from safety.

Man Utd's 18th-place position is their lowest after 10 top-flight games since 1986/87, when they were 20th. items.title: Villa boss Emery explains why he went down tunnel before full-time
items.excerpt: A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.
body: A prickly Unai Emery claimed he headed down the Old Trafford tunnel after Manchester United's late equaliser against his Aston Villa side because he thought the match was about to end.

Villa threw away two separate two-goal leads to draw 4-4 with United in a Super Sunday thriller - but the 97th-minute equaliser from Michael Carrick's side, scored by Patrick Dorgu, brought about a strange reaction from Emery.

The Villa manager was seen walking down the tunnel before the full-time whistle, with the match continuing for another two minutes before it ended. items.title: Hits and misses: Alisson back to his best while Chelsea go back to square one
items.excerpt: Liverpool hit three at Palace, with three £100m+ players - Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and, with an assist, Bradley Barcola - involved in the goals. But it was their goalkeeper Alisson who was Liverpool's best performer.
body: Liverpool hit three at Palace, with three £100m+ players - Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and, with an assist, Bradley Barcola - involved in the goals. But it was their goalkeeper Alisson who was Liverpool's best performer.

Crystal Palace will be so frustrated because on another day, the narrative could have swung their way. But the brilliant Brazilian delivered in key moments in the game. Crystal Palace 1-3 Liverpool - Match report & highlights As it happened | Teams | Stats
His save from Daichi Kamada's volley was an exceptional reaction stop. Two minutes later Liverpool took the lead.

Alisson was then at full stretch to push away Adam Wharton's header to ensure Liverpool went into the break with the advantage. And on 77 minutes, with the score 2-0, he prevented Yeremy Pino from setting up a grandstand finish by shutting down the angle to save the one-on-one.

items.title: Five-star Falkirk thump sorry Hearts to move up to third
items.excerpt: Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts' 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.
body: Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts' 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken's beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell's double.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995. items.title: Tepid Chelsea beaten by Sunderland who move off bottom
items.excerpt: Chelsea put in a tepid performance as Sunderland lifted themselves off the bottom of the Premier League table with a 1-0 win that eases the pressure on under-fire manager Regis Le Bris.
body: Chelsea put in a tepid performance as Sunderland lifted themselves off the bottom of the Premier League table with a 1-0 win that eases the pressure on under-fire manager Regis Le Bris.

Xabi Alonso's side were second-best throughout. None of their midfield attack won a duel or a tackle in the opening 20 minutes, while Sunderland's fight was best shown through Brian Brobbey's efforts up front.
The Dutch international smashed his way through Chelsea centre-backs Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill in a brutal first half - coming close to scoring twice, before eventually getting his rewards.

Ten minutes before half-time, he rolled past Colwill with immense strength to win a penalty, which Enzo Le Fee converted. Colwill was then taken off at half-time. items.title: Bournemouth win at Ipswich to record eight straight victories
items.excerpt: Bournemouth made it eight wins in a row in all competitions as they continued their charge up the Premier League table with a 2-1 win at Ipswich.
body: Bournemouth made it eight wins in a row in all competitions as they continued their charge up the Premier League table with a 2-1 win at Ipswich.
Evanilson scored for the fifth Premier League game running when taking advantage of a shocking error from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton, who tried to dribble around the striker.

Bournemouth arrived in Suffolk eager to complete an almost perfect month since the last international break with another three points and Alex Scott returned to the bench in another boost for Marco Rose.
Ipswich started the second half in nightmare fashion in a very sloppy overall performance, with the Cherries given a helping hand to score again after 27 seconds.

items.title: Sage in big trouble as Palace hit rock-bottom after defeat to Liverpool
items.excerpt: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park to inflict a fourth consecutive Premier League defeat on the hosts and leave Pierre Sage in a perilous position with his side bottom of the table.
body: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 at Selhurst Park to inflict a fourth consecutive Premier League defeat on the hosts and leave Pierre Sage in a perilous position with his side bottom of the table.

Eddie Nketiah pulled a goal back from the spot for Palace with the last kick of the game, but the damage was already done after Alexis Mac Allister and Florian Wirtz struck for Liverpool either side of half time before Alexander Isak added a third late on.

Liverpool secured a much-needed result following back-to-back defeats at Arsenal and Fenerbahce.
